decisions.reason: The same message independently establishes the cover page-number rule, which is already represented by the candidate's INTRODUCE Event. The table-of-contents correction does not require any additional change to that rule.
Correcting table-of-contents page numbers does not change the policy for visible white space at article ends.
Table-of-contents pagination accuracy does not alter the required rendering sharpness of advertisements.
The table-of-contents correction does not change the article body typeface or readability constraint.
Final pagination may reflect the included articles, but the instruction to correct table-of-contents page numbers does not change which articles must be included or who places them.
Using correct finalized pagination in the table of contents does not change the independent requirements for balanced two-page spreads and flipbook compatibility.
The table-of-contents correction does not alter the tribute page's required placement near the end of the magazine.
Table-of-contents page-number accuracy has no necessary effect on article image-quality remediation.
Correcting table-of-contents pagination does not modify the magazine's polished, modern, brand-aligned visual style.
The pagination correction applies to table-of-contents content and does not change the requirement to deliver a digital flipbook.
The table-of-contents correction neither resumes nor changes the deferred print-ready output requirement.
Correcting table-of-contents page numbers does not change the specified source from which articles are obtained.
